parts.text: 3 The salt sodium chloride, NaCl, can be prepared in the laboratory by different methods. method 1 Burning sodium metal is placed into a gas jar of chlorine gas. Solid sodium chloride is formed. 2Na + Cl 2 2NaCl method 2 Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to a known volume of aqueous sodium hydroxide in the presence of an indicator until a neutral solution is formed.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the mass of sodium chloride formed when excess burning sodium metal is placed into 960 cm 3 of chlorine gas at room temperature and pressure in method 1. mass = ...................................................... g [3]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) In Figure 3.1, complete the dot-and-cross diagram of the ions in sodium chloride. Give the charges on the ions. Figure 3.1 [3]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
M1 8 crosses in second shell of Na
M2 7 dots and 1 cross in third shell of Cl
M3 positive ‘+’ charge on Na on correct answer line AND negative ‘–‘ charge on Cl on correct answer line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Molten and aqueous sodium chloride are separately electrolysed using inert electrodes.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Complete Table 3.1 to show the name of the product formed at the cathode during the electrolysis of different forms of sodium chloride. Table 3.1 form of sodium chloride name of product formed at the cathode molten dilute aqueous solution concentrated aqueous solution [3]

ms.text:
